newsitem.title: CHINA: China car supply seen outstripping demand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China car supply seen outstripping demand in 1997.

text.p: China's supply of automobiles is seen far outstripping demand in 1997, with the market expected to continue its lacklustre performance, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
Demand for cars in China was forecast to hit 1.66 million vehicles next year, up about eight percent from this year, Xinhua said.
That would compare with a supply of about 2.0 million units on the nation's market, with 250,000 vehicles left unsold from this year, the agency said.

"Next year's auto market will be better than this year's, but...prospects of an all-round recovery are still dim," Xinhua quoted Liu Chanfu, deputy general manager of the China Automotive Industry Corp, as saying.
"Many automobile manufacturers or marketers are finding it hard to extricate themselves from the mess that has accumulated over the past three years," Xinhua said without elaborating.
Domestic car makers would turn out 1.65 million new motor vehicles next year, compared to a estimated 1.55 million this year, it said.
Imports could shoot up 50 percent to 120,000 vehicles next year from the projected 80,000 units this year, it said.
"Cars used by officials or businesses have been competitive, with the former being a major force in the auto market," Xinhua said, adding that private cars were still a fledgling market.
Many government officials and businessmen prefer imported luxury cars.
"The structure of purchasing automobiles, which is heavily institutional, is unlikely to change," it said.
Sales of compact cars had grown by 23.27 percent in January to September this year while van sales had gone up by 8.46 percent, it said.
Sales of heavy and light-duty trucks would remain sluggish next year, it said but gave no further details.
